world.h: Saudi forces destroy Houthi missile aimed at Riyadh
world.b: Al Jazeera's live coverage: Saudi forces say they destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh.
world.title: Saudi forces destroy Houthi ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh

national.h: Severe flooding hits Four Corners region
national.b: Historic flooding along the San Juan River forced evacuations and rooftop rescues, with more rain expected through the weekend.
national.title: Severe flooding hits Four Corners region, more expected through the weekend

national.h: Kirk case defense says it needs years to prepare
national.b: Defense attorneys for Tyler Robinson, charged with aggravated murder in Charlie Kirk's killing, say they need years to prepare for trial. A judge scheduled a hearing to set a trial date.
national.title: Defense attorneys in case over Charlie Kirk's killing say they need years to prepare for trial

national.h: Minnesota: feds stopped sharing Good, Pretti evidence
national.b: Minnesota officials say the Trump administration stopped sharing evidence in the killings of Renee Good and Pretti during the Minneapolis immigration crackdown. The state still seeks officers' phones and key recordings.

national.h: Bird flu rages on Utah mink farm
national.b: ProPublica reports bird flu is spreading on a mink farm, which experts say could help the virus adapt to humans. Officials declined to test workers despite CDC guidance urging monitoring.
national.title: Bird Flu Is Raging on a Mink Farm. It Could Spark a Human Pandemic, Experts Say, but Officials Won’t Act.

national.h: USDA moves to fight SNAP card theft
national.b: The USDA issued a proposed rule Friday to fight theft from outdated SNAP benefit cards, after ProPublica reported on millions in stolen benefits. The rule had been in the works since 2023.
national.title: After Millions in Stolen SNAP Benefits, Trump Administration Moves to Fight Theft

politics.h: Pentagon calls Confucius Institutes a security threat
politics.b: Defense Secretary Hegseth said the Pentagon added the Chinese-backed Confucius Institutes to its list of institutions that threaten national security.
politics.title: Pentagon designates Confucius Institutes a national security threat

politics.h: Trump eases Canada tariffs as Collins seeks help
politics.b: Trump exempted some Canadian imports from his 50% tariffs. Sen. Susan Collins, in a tight race with Troy Jackson, said she had raised the toll on Maine farmers and businesses with top trade officials.
politics.title: Seeking to help Collins in Maine, Trump exempts some Canadian imports from his 50% tariffs

politics.h: Trump administration sues over Alaska Senate race
politics.b: The administration filed a lawsuit to block certification if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses to Democrat Mary Peltola while another candidate with the same name is on the ballot.
politics.title: Trump administration files lawsuit to block possible Democratic win

politics.h: Paxton trust gave $600K to convicted fraudster's firm
politics.b: ProPublica finds Ken Paxton's trust was far from blind, investing $600,000 in a company built by Scott Sherman, according to previously unreleased impeachment records.
politics.title: Ken Paxton’s Trust Gave a $600,000 Infusion to a Convicted Fraudster’s Company

politics.h: 2 ex-FBI officials charged over Hunter Biden laptop
politics.b: Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, former leaders of a disbanded foreign election interference task force, are charged with making false statements. They appeared in federal court in Washington.

politics.h: Supreme Court lets N.H. bar student IDs for voting
politics.b: The Supreme Court allowed New Hampshire to fully ban student IDs as voter identification in the midterms, citing the principle against changing rules close to Election Day. Justice Jackson dissented.

politics.h: RFK Jr. adviser Calley Means resigns
politics.b: Means stepped down amid growing MAHA discontent over what backers call slow progress on food and glyphosate.

politics.h: Omar to move out of DC home after search
politics.b: Rep. Ilhan Omar said she will move out of her Washington home after a federal search and is "confident" she did nothing wrong, as prosecutors probe her family's immigration paperwork.

international.h: Israeli raids hit 15 West Bank towns
international.b: Israeli forces raided at least 15 towns in the northern West Bank, including Nablus, Jenin, Tubas and Qalqilya, detaining dozens of Palestinians after a Hebron attack killed two soldiers.
international.title: Israel raids towns, detains dozens of Palestinians in occupied West Bank

international.h: Argentine judge drops Milei crypto probe
international.b: Judge Marcelo Martinez de Giorgi ended an inquiry into President Milei's role in the launch of the $Libra token, ruling the events were not a criminal offence.
international.title: Argentinian judge drops fraud investigation into Milei over crypto scandal

international.h: Typhoon Champi kills 1, injures 350 in Taiwan
international.b: Typhoon Champi cut power to thousands of households in Taiwan and forced more than 4,300 people to evacuate. It is heading toward China and Japan, cancelling hundreds of flights.
international.title: Typhoon Champi hits Taiwan, killing one and injuring hundreds

international.h: Ministers warn US against new Iran attacks
international.b: Foreign ministers from the UK, France, Germany, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Egypt and Italy met in Turkiye on the Strait of Hormuz and cautioned the US against further attacks on Iran.
international.title: European, Middle East ministers urge US-Iran diplomacy, not new attacks

international.h: White House: Melania Trump secured Oleshky truce
international.b: The White House says Melania Trump secured a ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky. A Ukrainian official said it would be established soon, and the Kremlin said the military was coordinating the timing.

international.h: Gunmen kill 7 at church funeral in Jordan
international.b: Gunmen opened fire at a church during a funeral in Karak, killing seven and wounding 34. The government said investigations are under way and did not say whether any attackers were caught.

international.h: Greece bans social media for under-15s
international.b: Greece's governing New Democracy party used its majority to pass a ban on social media for children under 15, with no other party backing it. It takes effect January 1, 2027.

international.h: South Korea invites North to border talks
international.b: Seoul invited Pyongyang to military talks to confirm the land demarcation line, restore military communication lines and prevent accidental clashes, as border activity increases.

Whether Israel's ultra-Orthodox minority should serve in the military has come to dominate the campaign ahead of the October 27 election. An estimated 80,000 Haredi men aged 18 to 24 are avoiding service.

international.h: Gunmen attack Israeli troops near Telem
international.b: The Israeli military said it killed two gunmen who attacked a reserve battalion near the Telem settlement in the occupied West Bank. At least six soldiers were injured, two of them critically.

international.h: Venezuelans hold first national protest in two years
international.b: Protesters demanded a date for elections to choose a successor to Nicolas Maduro, who was captured by US forces in January. Acting President Delcy Rodriguez has promised a vote.
Demonstrators across Poland marked six years since the near-total abortion ban, calling for free and legal access.

international.h: Rare unrest in Tunis as police clash with protesters
international.b: Police fired tear gas in the Tunis suburb of Ettadhamen after the death of a man detained on suspicion of drug dealing.

international.h: Grenade drill sparked deadly Alberta base fire
international.b: Canada's army says a grenade launcher exercise sparked the fire that killed four people at the Wainwright base in Alberta, and high winds spread the flames.

business.h: Business activity stays near five-year high
business.b: S&P Global's purchasing managers' index signaled strong growth in October with more hiring plans, but prices companies pay and charge keep surging.
business.title: There's reason to believe the private sector economy is actually doing pretty well

business.h: Treasury proposes curbs on tech investment in China
business.b: Treasury proposed a rule expanding limits on U.S. investments in sensitive technologies in China and other adversaries, including Russia, Iran, North Korea and Cuba.
business.title: Treasury proposes rule to curb high-tech investments in China and other adversaries

business.b: Premiums for employer-sponsored insurance rose 9% this year on average, a KFF survey finds, and are on track to rise again as open enrollment begins.
business.title: Open enrollment is here and the cost of employer health plans is going up — again

business.h: IEA chief warns of hard winter for Europe
business.b: IEA head Fatih Birol warned Europe is particularly vulnerable to Hormuz energy disruptions and will likely face rising LNG costs in the coming months, even if peace returns to the Gulf.

business.h: Holiday airfares soar with jet fuel near record
business.b: Experts expect holiday airfares to be the highest in years as airlines scramble to cover jet fuel costs that are close to an all-time high in the U.S.

business.h: Tech stocks tumble on AI spending worries
business.b: Tech stocks posted their steepest drop since June and the S&P 500 slid 1.21%, its biggest fall since late July, as investors fretted over AI spending.

sports.h: Bears flagged for rare illegal forward handing
sports.b: The Bears became the first team in 16 years to be called for illegal forward handing, on a trick play against the Patriots that lost five yards.

sports.h: Utah DT Jamal Wallace suspended after arrest
sports.b: Utah suspended Wallace indefinitely after his arrest on suspicion of distributing intimate images. A woman also accused him of rape, an affidavit shows.

sports.h: MLB heads toward a likely lockout
sports.b: Players and owners are sparring over a possible salary cap as the labor deal nears expiration, raising the odds of a work stoppage that would affect free agency and 2027.

goodnews.h: WHO starts Ebola vaccine trial in DR Congo
goodnews.b: The WHO says participants in a clinical trial were vaccinated with the Ervebo vaccine in Bunia, in Ituri province, the epicentre of the Ebola outbreak.

local.h: 5 men charged in 2 Manhattan manhole cases
local.b: Police arrested five men on trespassing and other charges in two separate manhole cases in Upper Manhattan. Two told police they went into the sewer looking for jewelry.
local.title: 5 men charged with trespassing in 2 Manhattan manhole cases

local.h: Mamdani extends ban on new street fairs
local.b: The administration is extending a decades-old moratorium on new street fairs through 2027, citing NYPD overtime. Fairs held this year can still renew.
local.title: Mamdani extends ban on permits for new street fairs due to NYPD overtime

local.h: Countdown clocks coming to NYC bus stops
local.b: The city transportation department struck a deal to bring countdown clocks to more bus stops, so riders across the five boroughs can see how long they'll wait.
local.title: Countdown clocks are coming to an NYC bus stop near you

periods.name: Overnight
periods.text: Partly cloudy, with a low around 43. North wind around 7 mph.

periods.name: Saturday
periods.text: Partly sunny, with a high near 64. North wind 5 to 7 mph becoming light and variable  in the morning.

periods.name: Saturday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 42. Light and variable wind becoming northwest around 5 mph.

periods.name: Sunday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 68. Light and variable wind.

periods.name: Sunday Night
periods.text: Clear, with a low around 46. West wind around 6 mph.
